newsitem.title: USA: Hotel owners sue Ritz-Carlton, Marriott.
newsitem.headline: Hotel owners sue Ritz-Carlton, Marriott.

text.p: The owners of four Ritz-Carlton hotels said Tuesday they have filed a lawsuit against Marriott International Inc and the Ritz-Carlton Hotel Co, alleging fraudulent conveyance in connection with Marriott's 1995 acquisition of the hotel chain's assets.

The lawsuit was filed by owners of Ritz-Carlton hotels in New York, Washington, Houston and Aspen, Colo. It seeks $250 million, plus punitive damages. It was filed in the New York State Supreme Court.

Earlier this week, those hotels were stripped of the Ritz-Carlton name after the abrupt termination over the weekend of the relationship between Ritz-Carlton Hotel Co LLC and Sheik Abdul Aziz Bin Ibrahim al Ibrahim, the owner of the hotels.

Ritz-Carlton, which puts its name on hotels it is hired to run, said in recent days that it had ended 2-1/2 years of disputes with the sheik's holding company by pulling out of the hotels and filing the lawsuit.

Ritz-Carlton had alleged that the owners, Al Anwa USA Inc, a holding company controlled by al Ibrahim, owed more than $4 million in back pay and fees to the management company, hand meddled in the management of the properties and refused to make improvements.

In the latest lawsuit, the four hotels contend that the acquisition was intentionally structured to shift assets out of Ritz-Carlton Hotel Co potentially to avoid paying more than $200 million in restitution and damages stemming from a 1995 federal court action they had filed against the company.

"The acquisition of Ritz-Carlton by Marriott was effected through a byzantine set of transactions that was designed to mask the fact that Ritz-Carlton did not receive any consideration for the transfer of its assets to Marriott," said Abdul Aziz Al-Shehail, who was described in a news release as a special adviser to the investors.

"By dispersing and scattering the proceeds of that sale to a variety of people, Ritz-Carlton and Marriott caused the property of the entity against which our federal suit had been filed to effectively vanish," he added.
In the 1995 complaint, the four partnerships contended that the company mismanaged the properties and misappropriated tens of millions of dollars.
That complaint has been pending since January 1995.
The partnerships bringing the lawsuit are N.Y. Overnight Partners LP, D.C. Overnight Partners LP, Savanah Limited Partnership and New Remington Partners.
Those are the same partnerships named in the Ritz-Carlton Hotel lawsuit.
Neither Marriott, Ritz-Carlton, nor the partnerships were immediately available for comment.
Marriott owns a 49 percent stake in Ritz-Carlton Hotels Co.
Marriott spokesman Tom Marder said later Tuesday that "we haven't seen any complaint, and as such, we can't comment on something we haven't seen."
